title: Gus and the Vet
lines: Gus has a tan cat. It has a cut.
"A vet can fix a cut," said Mom.
"Vets fix pets. We can get in the van."
Mom gets the van, but the cat hid!
Gus got it and set it on his lap.
The vet has a wet rag. She rubs it.
"You have a big, tan cat," she said.
The cat naps on his lap in the van.

questions.listenFor: Someone who fixes pets. Mom says it in lines three and four. This is the word the whole story rests on, so it is worth checking they have it.

questions.ask: How do you know the cat did not want to go?
questions.listenFor: The cat hid when Mom got the van. That is evidence, not a guess - have them find the line and read it back.

questions.ask: Which part will you draw — the cat hiding, or the cat asleep on Gus?
questions.listenFor: Either. Line five is the hiding; the last line is the nap. The reason matters more than the pick.
